Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The COREMERCH infrastructure is designed for resilience against common payment platform failures. Unlike conventional systems, this architecture is built on open-source tools that you control entirely. By utilizing Supabase for order management, you effectively sidestep the limitations imposed by traditional payment processors. This means you can operate your digital store without worrying about account freezes or service denials, particularly in regions where financial services are unreliable.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you begin deployment, gather the necessary components: a GitHub account for hosting, Google Apps Script for backend logic, and a NOWPayments account for cryptocurrency transactions. Ensure you have your digital products ready for upload and have established your branding elements. Additionally, familiarize yourself with the Sovereign Blueprint, which provides a detailed roadmap for setting up your stack efficiently. This preparation is crucial for a smooth deployment process.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Start by deploying your backend using GitHub Pages and Google Apps Script. This process should take about 4-6 hours if you follow the Sovereign Blueprint closely. Once your backend is operational, integrate NOWPayments to handle crypto transactions. Ensure to configure your product delivery method, utilizing services like Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for instant file access. Testing the payment and delivery functionality is essential before you go live.
Empower your digital store with complete infrastructure sovereignty.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

After testing your setup, it's time to go live. Share your store link widely, directing potential customers to your GitHub Pages site. Monitor the first transactions closely to ensure that payments are processed smoothly through NOWPayments. Utilize the webhook feature to handle confirmations automatically, streamlining your operations. This step is crucial for establishing trust with your customers and ensuring a seamless shopping experience.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your store is operational, focus on scaling up. Consider adding more products and leveraging Supabase's capabilities to manage inventory and track customer interactions. You can optimize your marketing strategies based on user behavior data collected through your store. If you're looking for a more robust solution, consider the Edge Commerce Stack, which offers enhanced features and end-to-end testing for greater reliability as you scale.

The difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 is not which one works — both work — it is which one fits your situation. Stack 01 is the right choice if you want to deploy yourself, you are comfortable with Google Workspace tools, and your initial volume is under 100 orders per day. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete Stack 01 build with full source code and step-by-step configuration. Stack 02 is the right choice if you want the deployment done for you, you need higher volume capacity, or you want email deliverability infrastructure configured from day one. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy Stack 02 under your accounts in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.

If you're looking for advanced options, consider the Edge Commerce Stack, which utilizes Cloudflare Pages and Workers for enhanced performance. This stack includes a fully configured backend and faster transaction processing, ideal for growing your digital store. Explore more at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html for additional resources.
Your Deployment Checklist

Read the Sovereign Blueprint before you start configuring anything — understanding the complete architecture before touching any settings prevents the most common configuration mistakes. Create all required accounts first: NOWPayments, Cloudflare or GitHub, Supabase or Google account, Resend or Gmail. Then configure the backend with all credentials before deploying it. Then deploy the backend and confirm the endpoint is live. Then configure NOWPayments with the endpoint URL. Then build and deploy the storefront. Then configure your custom domain if using one. Then run the mainnet test. Then check the order database. Then — and only then — share the URL. The sequence is not arbitrary. Each step depends on the previous one.

Yes, both GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages can be used to host your digital product store. GitHub Pages is suitable for Stack 01, while Cloudflare Pages offers enhanced performance for Stack 02.
What are the benefits of using Supabase as my order database?

Supabase provides a powerful and flexible solution for managing your order data. It allows you to control your own data, ensuring privacy and reliability, which is essential when traditional payment processors are unavailable.
